subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation (Acme Corp)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme-corp.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 15:32:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation (Acme Corp)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned:

Pain points you described
- Multiple production incidents over the last quarter impacting inference availability (two incidents with multi-minute outages; one incident caused a fallback to a much lower-quality model).
- Need predictable latency and graceful degradation for customer-facing features (timeouts and poor fallbacks are hurting UX).
- Desire to avoid a single-region/blow-up scenario and to have clear SLOs/SLAs that map to business impact.

Current stack you shared
- Primary app in GCP us-central, internal routing to a mix of self-hosted GPUs + burst to third-party endpoints.
- No unified KV/prefix cache across regions today.
- Monitoring relies on internal dashboards and PagerDuty.

Success criteria you mentioned
- P95 latency under 300ms for standard prompts (with alerts for regressions).
- 99.9% availability for the inference endpoints used by checkout flows.
- Automatic, tested fallback path that preserves response quality where possible (not just a blank message).

Redwood capabilities relevant to this ask
- Regional routing + automatic fallback to compatible model variants (we can route to a smaller quantized model or to a different region and still preserve prompt semantics).
- Prefix/KV caching to reduce cost and surface-time for repeated prompts; optional cross-region cache replication patterns.
- SLA templates and runbooks for failover testing; we can provide a draft SLA and an incident playbook for your SREs.

Attachments I’m sharing
- redwood-sla-draft.pdf (initial SLA template tuned to your success criteria)
- runbook-fallback-strategy.md (high-level failover options + pros/cons)

Proposed next steps
1) Tech deep-dive with your SREs and our infra team — 60–90m to walk through architecture, routing policy, and KV/cache approach. Suggested slots: Tue 12/1 or Thu 12/3.
2) We’ll update the SLA to reflect the 99.9% availability target and include measurable latency SLOs.
3) Redwood will produce a short mutually agreed action plan (MAP) with rollout milestones and a tested failover drill.

If that all looks right I’ll lock in the tech deep-dive and ask Marissa to join for the SLA/runbook conversation.

Thanks —
Ben

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation (Acme Corp)

Ben — thanks for the summary, this is helpful and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifying Qs from our side before the tech deep-dive: 

1) Fallback behavior: when you refer to "compatible model variants," can you confirm whether that means you can serve a quantized smaller model that keeps semantic fidelity (we need to avoid hallucination/regression on billing-related prompts)? Any examples of prior customer configs would help.
2) Region failover: does Redwood support automatic regional failover at the edge (we'd like sub-30s failover for critical routes), and can we test failover without impacting production traffic?
3) Cross-region KV cache: we have some stateful prompt prefixes — is cross-region cache replication something you support or is the advice to accept higher cold-starts post-failover?
4) Cost: can you provide a ballpark delta between a primary-resident model + fallback smaller model vs. full multi-region dedicated replicas (we're evaluating both)?

I attached our security questionnaire (acme-security-questionnaire.pdf) — we’ll also want to see SOC2 evidence if we move forward.

We can do Tue 12/1 at 10am PT for the deep-dive. Confirmed attendees: Tom Reed (SRE), me (Platform lead), and one of our infra engineers.

— Sarah
Sarah Liu
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Corp
sarah.liu@acme-corp.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme-corp.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation (Acme Corp)

Sarah — great questions, answered inline below. We’ll cover details in the deep-dive but wanted to give a crisp summary so your team can prep.

1) Fallback model fidelity- We commonly deploy a smaller quantized variant (e.g., "redwood-small-q4" family) as a fallback. In practice for billing/accounting prompts we run a short eval suite pre-rollout to ensure parity on critical intents. Ops story:
  - We run canary/regression evals against your golden prompt set.
  - If quality degrades beyond an agreed threshold we route to a higher-quality model (with higher latency) rather than returning lower-quality text.
  - Attached runbook-fallback-strategy.md has an example eval threshold table.

2) Region failover- Redwood supports policy-driven routing (region, cost, latency, tier). Failover options:
  - Active-active with health checks + regional priorities (failover typically under ~30s for control-plane-level detection; for full traffic convergence plan on ~30–90s depending on DNS and client retries).
  - We can do a staged failover drill using canary traffic and traffic shadowing to test without impacting production.

3) Cross-region KV cache- Native strong cross-region KV replication is not automatic by default (consistency and cost trade-offs). Options:
  - Replicated cache layer (we can operate a managed replication pattern for critical prefixes) — higher cost but faster warm-up after failover.
  - Accept cold-start hits post-failover with warmed prefix seeding for the most-critical keys.
  - We'll present latency/cost trade-offs in the deep-dive.

4) Ballpark cost delta- Rough estimates (very high level):
  - Primary + fallback quantized model: ~30–40% below full multi-region dedicated replicas (lower infra cost, modest quality trade-offs).
  - Full multi-region dedicated replicas: higher cost but lowest failover latency and best quality parity.

Attachments: redwood-sla-draft.pdf, runbook-fallback-strategy.md (same as in initial mail). I’ll also pull SOC2 artifact links for you to review before the call.

Confirming Tue 12/1 at 10am PT for the technical deep-dive. Action items before the call:
- Ben/Jordan/Marissa: prepare a <45m architecture + failover runbook walkthrough and a ~15m Q&A.
- Acme: share any golden prompt set or critical intent list (we can use this for the canary/regression checks).

Looking forward —
Ben
